title: Candidate regions
subtitle: Regions whose bytes changed across the loaded dumps, ranked.
needDumps: Select at least 2 dumps of the same process to compare them.
idle: Run Consensus (Dumps panel) to rank the regions that changed across these dumps, or apply the filters below directly.
truncated: Truncated to the {{max}} best-ranked rows; narrow the filters to see the rest.
fallbackEntropyOnly: Too few dumps for trustworthy cross-dump variance — these rows were ranked on entropy alone and carry no byte classes.

empty.title: No regions matched.
empty.description: That is a result, not an error: most bytes of a process are invariant across a phase series. Widen the length range, lower the entropy threshold, or add a class.

filters.classesHint: Defaults to every non-invariant class — real key material is class-mixed.

table.caption: Ranked candidate regions
table.jumpTitle: Jump to this offset in the hex viewer
table.jumpUnavailable: Jump unavailable: this consensus was aligned across dumps, so the offset is a position in the aligned region set rather than an offset in any one dump.

legend.summary: What a candidate is, and what it is not
legend.honesty: A candidate is a region whose bytes CHANGED across the dumps you loaded. It is not a proven key: nothing here decrypts anything. Confirm one with the pcap oracle or a brute-force run before believing it.
legend.ranking: Rank comes from a weighted blend of the region's byte-class mix, its cross-dump variance, its own entropy and its length. Every component is on the row, so a rank can be recomputed by hand.
legend.coordinate: Offsets are in the comparison coordinate named by the alignment banner. Under flat file-offset alignment they are file offsets; under an aligned method they index the aligned span, not the file.

class.structural: Structural — low variance; lengths, counters, flags.
class.pointer: Pointer — medium variance; addresses moving with the heap.
class.key_candidate: Key Candidate — high variance; the band random key bytes fall in.
